title.en: Volume 123 Book of Later Zhou 25: Biographies 3 - Gao Xingzhou, An Shenqi, An Shenhui, An Shenxin, Li Congmin, Zheng Renhui, Zhang Yancheng, An Shuqian, Song Yanyun
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 周書14: 列傳三 高行周 安審琦 安審暉 安審信 李從敏 鄭仁誨 張彥成 安叔千 宋彥筠 Volume 123 Book of Later Zhou 25: Biographies 3 - Gao Xingzhou, An Shenqi, An Shenhui, An Shenxin, Li Congmin, Zheng Renhui, Zhang Yancheng, An Shuqian, Song Yanyun

sentences.zh: 高行周，字尚質，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou, courtesy name Shangzhi, was a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou, whose courtesy name was Shangzhi, came from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 生於媯州懷戎軍之雕窠裏。

translations.literal: He was born at Diaoke village in the Huairong garrison of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in Diaoke village, in the Huairong garrison district of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖順厲，世戍懷戎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shunli generation after generation garrisoned Huairong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shunli had for generations served as a garrison soldier at Huairong.

sentences.zh: 父思繼，昆仲三人，俱雄豪有武幹，聲馳朔方。

translations.literal: His father Siji, three brothers in all, were all heroic and had martial talent, their fame spreading through the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His father Siji and his two brothers were all bold warriors of proven martial skill, and their renown rang across the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 唐武皇之平幽州也，表劉仁恭為帥，仍留兵以戍之。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor of Tang pacified Youzhou, he appointed Liu Rengong as commander and still left troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong pacified Youzhou, he installed Liu Rengong as military governor and left a garrison force behind.

sentences.zh: 以思繼兄為先鋒都將、媯州刺史，思繼為中軍都將、順州刺史，思繼弟為後軍都將，昆仲分掌燕兵。

translations.literal: He appointed Siji's elder brother as vanguard commander and prefect of Guizhou, Siji as central army commander and prefect of Shunzhou, and Siji's younger brother as rear army commander; the brothers divided command of the Yan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Siji's elder brother became vanguard commander and prefect of Guizhou; Siji took the central army and the prefecture of Shunzhou; the youngest brother commanded the rear guard — between them the three brothers controlled the Yan region's military forces.

sentences.zh: 部下士伍，皆山北之豪也，仁恭深憚之。

translations.literal: The soldiers under their command were all magnates north of the mountains; Rengong deeply feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The men in their ranks were powerful northern chieftains, and Rengong viewed them with deep apprehension.

sentences.zh: 武皇將歸，私謂仁恭曰：「高先鋒兄弟，勢傾州府，為燕患者，必此族也，宜善籌之。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor was about to return, he privately said to Rengong: "The elder brother of the Gao vanguard and his kin — their power overwhelms the prefectures and districts; those who will afflict Yan must be this clan. You should plan carefully for them."
translations.idiomatic: Before Li Keyong withdrew, he took Rengong aside: "The Gao brothers command more power than your government can hold. They are the men who will become Yan's curse. You must deal with them wisely."

sentences.zh: 」久之，太原戍軍恣橫，思繼兄弟制之以法，所殺者多。

translations.literal: After a long time, the garrison troops from Taiyuan ran riot; the Siji brothers restrained them by law, and many were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In time the Taiyuan garrison grew insubordinate; the Siji brothers enforced discipline upon them, and many troopers were executed.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，詬讓仁恭，乃訴以高氏兄弟，遂並遇害。

translations.literal: The founder was angry and reproached Rengong; [Rengong] then accused the Gao brothers, and they all met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was furious and berated Rengong, who shifted blame to the Gao brothers — whereupon all three were killed.

sentences.zh: 仁恭因以先鋒子行珪為牙將，諸子並列帳下，厚撫之以慰其心。

translations.literal: Rengong thereupon made the vanguard's son Xinggui a guards officer; all the sons were placed under his banner, and he richly treated them to comfort their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong appointed the slain vanguard's son Xinggui to his personal guard and brought the surviving sons under his command, treating them generously to win their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時行周十餘歲，亦補職，在仁恭左右。

translations.literal: At that time Xingzhou was just over ten years old and also received an appointment, attending on Rengong's person.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou was then barely past ten; he too was given a post and remained at Rengong's side.

sentences.zh: 行珪別有傳，在《唐書》。

translations.literal: Xinggui has a separate biography in the Book of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui's biography appears separately in the Book of Tang.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗收燕，以行周隸明宗帳下，常與唐末帝分率牙兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took Yan, he placed Xingzhou under Emperor Mingzong's command; he often shared leadership of the guards with the Last Emperor of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong conquered Yan, Xingzhou was assigned to Mingzong's staff and often shared command of the guard corps with the future Last Emperor of Tang.

sentences.zh: 明宗征燕，率其下擁從。

translations.literal: When Mingzong campaigned against Yan, [Xingzhou] led his subordinates to escort and follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong marched on Yan, Xingzhou led his men in loyal attendance.

sentences.zh: 鄉人趙德鈞謂明宗曰：「行周心甚謹厚，必享貴位。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Zhao Dejun said to Mingzong: "Xingzhou's heart is very prudent and honest; he is sure to enjoy noble rank."
translations.idiomatic: A fellow northerner, Zhao Dejun, told Mingzong: "Xingzhou is remarkably steady and loyal. He is destined for high office."

sentences.zh: 」梁將劉鄩之據莘也，與太原軍對壘，旦夕轉鬥。

translations.literal: When the Liang general Liu Yan held Xin, he faced the Taiyuan army in pitched camps and fought day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang general Liu Yan held Xin, the armies of Liang and Taiyuan confronted each other and skirmished without cease.

sentences.zh: 嘗一日，兩軍成列，元行欽為敵軍追躡，劍中其面，血戰未解。

translations.literal: On one occasion the two armies drew up in formation; Yuan Xingqin was pursued by the enemy army, a sword struck his face, and he fought on in a bloody engagement without relief.
translations.idiomatic: Once, with both armies in battle order, Yuan Xingqin was chased by the enemy; a blade cut his face, yet he fought on, drenched in blood and unable to break free.

sentences.zh: 行周以麾下精騎突陣解之，行欽獲免。

translations.literal: Xingzhou with crack cavalry under his command charged the formation to rescue him; Xingqin escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou led his elite horsemen in a charge that broke the encirclement, and Xingqin was saved.

sentences.zh: 莊宗方寵行欽，召行周撫諭賞勞，而欲置之帳下，又念於明宗帳下已奪行欽，更取行周，恐傷其意，密令人以利祿誘之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was then favoring Xingqin, summoned Xingzhou to comfort, instruct, and reward him, and wished to place him in his personal staff; yet he also reflected that he had already taken Xingqin from Mingzong's staff — to take Xingzhou as well might wound Mingzong's feelings — so he secretly sent someone to entice him with profit and emoluments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong, who doted on Xingqin, summoned Xingzhou to praise and reward him and wished to add him to his own household guard. But he had already lured Xingqin away from Mingzong; to take Xingzhou too might offend Mingzong, so he secretly sent envoys to tempt Xingzhou with rank and riches.

sentences.zh: 行周辭曰：「總管用人，亦為國家，事總管猶事王也。

translations.literal: Xingzhou declined, saying: "The commander-in-chief employs men also for the state; serving the commander-in-chief is like serving the king."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhou refused: "My commander hires men for the nation's sake. To serve him is to serve the throne."

sentences.zh: 余家昆仲，脫難再生，承總管之厚恩，忍背之乎！

translations.literal: My family's brothers, escaping hardship and born anew, received the commander-in-chief's generous grace — how could we bear to betray him!
translations.idiomatic: My brothers and I were spared from extinction and given new life by his generosity. How could we turn our backs on him?

sentences.zh: 」及兩軍屯於河上，覘知梁軍自汴入楊村寨，明宗晨至斗門，設伏將邀之，眾寡不敵，反為所乘。

translations.literal: When the two armies camped on the Yellow River, [they] detected that the Liang army had entered Yangji village from Bian; Mingzong at dawn reached Doumen and set an ambush to intercept them; being outnumbered, they were instead overcome.
translations.idiomatic: While the two armies held the north bank of the Yellow River, scouts reported Liang troops advancing from Bian toward Yangji village. Mingzong reached Doumen at dawn to lay an ambush, but his force was too small and he was overrun instead.

sentences.zh: 時矛槊叢萃，勢甚危蹙。

translations.literal: At that time spears and halberds clustered thickly; the situation was extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Spears and halberds pressed in on every side; the situation was desperate.

sentences.zh: 行周聞之，出騎橫擊梁軍，遂得解去。

translations.literal: When Xingzhou heard of it, he led cavalry out in a lateral strike against the Liang army and thereby was able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the crisis, Xingzhou rode out and struck the Liang flank, allowing Mingzong's force to break away.

sentences.zh: 明宗之襲鄆州也，行周為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Mingzong assaulted Yanzhou, Xingzhou was the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong attacked Yanzhou, Xingzhou led the van.

sentences.zh: 會夜分澍雨，人無進誌，行周曰：「此天贊也，彼必無備。

translations.literal: It happened that at midnight a sudden rain fell; the men had no will to advance; Xingzhou said: "This is Heaven's aid — they are sure to be unprepared."
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a downpour began and the troops lost their appetite for advance. Xingzhou said: "Heaven favors us. The enemy will have no guard up."

sentences.zh: 」是夜，涉河入東城，比曙平之。

translations.literal: That night they crossed the river and entered the eastern city; by daybreak it was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That night they forded the river, took the eastern quarter, and by dawn the city was his.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平河南，累加檢校太保，領端州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, [Xingzhou] was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Guardian and made to hold the prefecture of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong subdued Henan, Xingzhou was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and appointed prefect of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 同光末，出守絳州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tongguang era, he went out to guard Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of the Tongguang reign, he was sent to defend Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，特深委遇。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, [Xingzhou] received especially deep trust and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong acceded, Xingzhou enjoyed his exceptional trust.

sentences.zh: 天成中，從王晏球圍定州，敗王都，擒禿諾，皆有功。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, he followed Wang Yanqiu in besieging Dingzhou, defeated Wang Du, captured Tuo Nuo — in all he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng period he joined Wang Yanqiu's siege of Dingzhou, helped defeat Wang Du, and captured Tuo Nuo — winning distinction in each action.

sentences.zh: 賊平，遷潁州團練使。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was transferred to be regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended, he was made regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長興初，以北邊鄰戎王，用為振武節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, because the northern border neighbored the Rong and Wang tribes, he was employed as military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changxing, because the northern frontier bordered Rong and Wang tribal powers, he was appointed military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 明年，以河西用軍，移鎮延安。

translations.literal: The next year, because troops were deployed in the Hexi region, he was shifted to govern Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with campaigns underway in the Hexi, he was reassigned to Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，改潞州節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, he was changed to military governor of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Qingtai era he became military governor of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉祖建義於太原，唐末帝命張敬達征之，行周與符彥卿為左右排陣使。

translations.literal: When the Ancestor of Jin raised righteousness at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor of Tang ordered Zhang Jingda to campaign against him; Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing were left and right array marshals.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Later Jin rebelled at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor sent Zhang Jingda against him, with Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing as his left and right wing commanders.

sentences.zh: 契丹主入援太原也，行周、彥卿引騎拒之，尋為契丹所敗，遂與敬達保晉安寨，累月救軍不至。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sovereign came to relieve Taiyuan, Xingzhou and Yanqing led cavalry to resist; soon they were defeated by the Khitan; thereupon together with Jingda they held Jin'an Stockade, month after month with no relief army arriving.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan khan marched to relieve Taiyuan, Xingzhou and Yanqing met him with cavalry but were soon routed. They fell back to Jin'an Stockade with Jingda, where they waited months for reinforcements that never came.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠欲圖敬達，行周知之，引壯士護之。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan wished to plot against Jingda; Xingzhou knew of it and led stalwart warriors to protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yang Guangyuan meant to harm Jingda, Xingzhou gathered trusted warriors to guard him.

sentences.zh: 敬達性戇，不知其營護，謂人曰：「行周每踵余後，其意何也？

translations.literal: Jingda was blunt by nature and did not know of his protection; he said to others: "Xingzhou always follows on my heels — what is his intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingda was obtuse and unaware of the protection; he complained, "Why does Xingzhou dog my every step?"

sentences.zh: 」繇是不復敢然，敬達遂為光遠所害。

translations.literal: Thereby [Yang] no longer dared to act so; [yet] Jingda was ultimately killed by Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang no longer dared act openly, but Jingda was nevertheless murdered by Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉祖入洛，令行周還藩，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor entered Luoyang, he ordered Xingzhou to return to his fief and added the title of Grand Councillor of the State Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu entered Luoyang, Xingzhou was sent back to his command with the added rank of Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 晉祖都汴，以行周為西京留守，未幾，移鄴都。

translations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor made his capital at Bian, he made Xingzhou Western Capital regent; before long, he was moved to the Ye capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu established his court at Bian, Xingzhou became regent of the Western Capital, then was soon transferred to Ye.

sentences.zh: 晉祖幸鄴，會安從進叛，命行周為襄州行營都部署。

translations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor visited Ye, it happened that An Congjin rebelled; he appointed Xingzhou as overall deployer of the Xiangzhou field camp.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozu's visit to Ye, An Congjin rebelled; Xingzhou was named supreme field commander for the Xiangzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，平定漢南。

translations.literal: The next autumn, the south of Han was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn the Han River southlands were pacified.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，加兼侍中，移鎮睢陽。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor of Jin succeeded, [Xingzhou] was given the additional title of Palace Attendant and shifted to garrison Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chudi succeeded, Xingzhou was made concurrent Palace Attendant and transferred to Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 開運初，從幸澶淵，拒敵於河上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun, he followed the imperial progress to Chanzhou and resisted the enemy on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun he accompanied the emperor to Chanzhou and held the enemy at the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，代景延廣為侍衛親軍都指揮使，移鄆州節度使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he replaced Jing Yanguang as commander of the imperial guard and personal armies and was moved to military governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the capital, Xingzhou replaced Jing Yanguang as commander of the palace guard and was made military governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時李彥韜為侍衛都虞候，可否在己。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yantao was chief military adviser of the guard; approval and denial rested with him alone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yantao served as chief adjutant of the guard and controlled every decision himself.

sentences.zh: 行周雖典禁兵，心遊事外，退朝歸第，門宇翛然，賓友過從，但引滿而已。

translations.literal: Although Xingzhou oversaw the forbidden troops, his mind roamed outside affairs; returning home after court, his gate and courtyard were serene; when guests and friends came and went, he merely raised a full cup, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Though nominally in charge of the palace armies, Xingzhou kept his mind elsewhere. After court he retired to a quiet household; when friends visited, he merely filled their cups and his own.

sentences.zh: 尋改歸德軍節度使，以李守貞代掌兵柄，許行周歸藩。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to military governor of the Guide Army; Li Shouzhen was substituted to wield military authority; Xingzhou was permitted to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made military governor of Guide, with Li Shouzhen taking the guard command while Xingzhou was allowed to return to his province.

sentences.zh: 晉軍降於中渡也，少帝命行周與符彥卿同守澶州。

translations.literal: When the Jin army surrendered at Zhongdu Ford, the Young Emperor ordered Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing jointly to hold Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin armies surrendered at Zhongdu Ford, Chudi ordered Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing to hold Chanzhou together.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，召赴京師，會草寇攻宋州急，遣行周歸鎮。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, [he] was summoned to the capital; it happened that bandits urgently attacked Songzhou; [the court] sent Xingzhou back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took Bian, Xingzhou was called to court, but raiders were pressing Songzhou hard, so he was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·高懷德傳》：杜重威降契丹，京東諸州群盜大起，懷德堅壁清野，敵不能入，行周率兵歸鎮，敵遂解去。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Gao Huaide in the History of Song: When Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan, bandits rose in great numbers throughout the eastern capital region. Huaide shut the gates and cleared the countryside so the enemy could not enter. Xingzhou led troops back to his command, and the enemy then withdrew.)]
translations.idiomatic: (History of Song, Biography of Gao Huaide: After Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan, brigands rose across the eastern provinces. Huaide sealed his walls and stripped the countryside bare so raiders could not penetrate. When Xingzhou marched back to his post, the enemy lifted the siege.)]

sentences.zh: 及契丹主死於欒城，契丹將蕭翰立許王李從益知南朝軍國事，遣死士召行周，辭之以疾，退謂人曰：「衰世難輔，況兒戲乎！」

translations.literal: When the Khitan sovereign died at Luancheng, the Khitan general Xiao Han installed Prince Xu Li Congyi to oversee the Southern Dynasty's military and state affairs, and sent death-sworn men to summon Xingzhou; he declined on grounds of illness and withdrew, saying to others: "A declining age is hard to support — moreover, this is child's play!"
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan emperor died at Luancheng, the Khitan general Xiao Han installed Prince Xu Li Congyi to govern the southern realm's military and civil affairs and sent sworn agents to summon Xingzhou. He pleaded illness and later told others, "A dying age is not worth serving — and this is mere child's play besides!"

sentences.zh: 子懷德，皇朝駙馬都尉、宋州節度使。

translations.literal: His son Huaide, in the present dynasty imperial son-in-law and military governor of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaide served the present dynasty as imperial son-in-law and military governor of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 安審琦，字國瑞，其先沙陀部人也。

translations.literal: An Shenqi, courtesy name Guorui; his ancestors were of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: An Shenqi, whose courtesy name was Guorui, came from Shatuo stock.

sentences.zh: 祖山盛，朔州牢城都校，贈太傅。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shansheng was garrison commander of the prison fort at Shuozhou, posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shansheng had been garrison commander of the Shuozhou prison fort and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 父金全，安北都護、振武軍節度使，累贈太師，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Jinquan, Protector-General of the Pacified North and military governor of the Zhenwu Army, was repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor; the Book of Tang has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinquan had served as Protector-General of the Pacified North and military governor of Zhenwu, was posthumously raised to Grand Preceptor, and has a biography in the Book of Tang.

sentences.zh: 審琦性驍果，善騎射，幼以良家子事莊宗為義直軍使，遷本軍指揮使。

translations.literal: Shenqi was fierce and resolute by nature, skilled at riding and archery; in youth as a good-family son he served Emperor Zhuangzong as commissioner of the Righteous and Upright Army, and was promoted to commander of that army.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi was bold and decisive, an expert horseman and archer. As a youth of good family he entered Zhuangzong's service as commissioner of the Righteous and Upright Army and rose to command that corps.

sentences.zh: 天成初，唐末帝由潞邸出鎮河中，奏審琦為牙兵都校，未幾，入為歸化指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, the Last Emperor of Tang left the Prince of Lu residence to govern Hezhong and memorialized Shenqi as chief guards officer; before long, [Shenqi] entered [court] as commander of the Submissive and Transformed [Army].
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng, when the future Last Emperor left his princely estate at Lu to govern Hezhong, he recommended Shenqi as chief of his guard. Soon afterward Shenqi was summoned to court as commander of the Submissive and Transformed Army.

sentences.zh: 王師伐蜀，充行營馬軍都指揮使，及凱旋，改龍武右廂都校，領富州刺史。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, he served as commander of the field camp's cavalry; upon triumphant return, he was changed to colonel of the Right Dragon Martial Guards and held the prefecture of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Shu he commanded the field army's cavalry. After the victory he became colonel of the Right Dragon Martial Guards and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，為捧聖指揮使，領順化軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, he was commander of the Upholding the Sage [Army] and held the military governorship of the Shunhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Qingtai he became commander of the Upholding the Sage Army and military governor of Shunhua.

sentences.zh: 其年鎮邢州，兼北面行營排軍陣使，從張敬達圍太原。

translations.literal: That year he garrisoned Xingzhou and concurrently served as northern frontier field camp array marshal, following Zhang Jingda in besieging Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was posted to Xingzhou as northern frontier array marshal and joined Zhang Jingda's siege of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及楊光遠舉晉安寨降於晉祖，審琦亦預焉。

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan raised Jin'an Stockade in surrender to the Jin Ancestor, Shenqi also took part.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guangyuan surrendered Jin'an Stockade to Gaozu, Shenqi was among those who followed.

sentences.zh: 晉祖踐阼，加檢校太傅、同平章事，充天平軍節度使兼侍衛馬步軍都指揮使，旋以母喪起復。

translations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor ascended the throne, [Shenqi] was given acting Grand Tutor and Grand Councillor of the State Chancery, made military governor of the Tianping Army and commander of the palace cavalry and infantry; soon after, on his mother's mourning he was recalled from leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Shenqi was made acting Grand Tutor and Grand Councillor, military governor of Tianping, and commander of the palace horse and foot. He was soon recalled from mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 天福三年，就加檢校太尉，尋改晉昌軍節度使、京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, he was further given acting Grand Commandant; before long he was changed to military governor of the Jinchang Army and metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu he was promoted to acting Grand Commandant, then reassigned as military governor of Jinchang and metropolitan magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 七年，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was shifted to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor of Jin succeeded, [Shenqi] was given acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chudi succeeded, Shenqi was made acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 開運末，朝廷以北戎入寇，以審琦為北面行營馬軍左右廂都指揮使，與諸將會兵於洺州。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, because the northern barbarians invaded, the court made Shenqi commander of both left and right wings of the northern frontier field camp cavalry, and with the various generals he assembled troops at Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaiyun, with northern tribes raiding the frontier, the court appointed Shenqi commander of both wings of the northern field cavalry and marched with other generals to Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而敵騎大至，時皇甫遇、慕容彥超亦預其行，乃率所部兵與敵戰於安陽河上。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy cavalry arrived in great force; at that time Huangfu Yu and Murong Yanchao also took part in the expedition; thereupon he led the troops under his command to fight the enemy on the Anyang River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enemy horsemen arrived in force. Huangfu Yu and Murong Yanchao were also on the campaign, and Shenqi led his troops into battle on the Anyang River.

sentences.zh: 時遇馬為流矢所中，勢已危蹙，諸將相顧，莫有敢救者。

translations.literal: At that time Yu's horse was struck by a stray arrow; the situation was already extremely perilous; the generals looked at one another, and none dared to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's horse was hit by a stray arrow and the situation turned desperate. The generals exchanged glances, but none dared advance to his aid.

sentences.zh: 審琦謂首將張從恩曰：「皇甫遇等未至，必為敵騎所圍，若不急救，則為擒矣。

translations.literal: Shenqi said to the chief general Zhang Cong'en: "Huangfu Yu and the others have not yet arrived — they are sure to be surrounded by enemy cavalry; if we do not rescue them at once, they will be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi told the chief commander Zhang Cong'en, "Huangfu Yu and the others have not yet broken through. The enemy cavalry will encircle them. If we do not rescue them now, they will be taken."

sentences.zh: 」從恩曰：「敵勢甚盛，無以枝梧，將軍獨往何益？

translations.literal: Cong'en said: "The enemy's force is very strong; there is no way to resist — what good is it if the general goes alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en replied, "The enemy is too strong to hold off. What good can you do going alone?"

sentences.zh: 」審琦曰：「成敗命也，若不濟，與之俱死，假令失此二將，何面目以見天子！

translations.literal: Shenqi said: "Success or failure is fate; if we do not succeed, we die with them. Supposing we lose these two generals — with what face could we see the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi said, "Victory or defeat is heaven's decree. If we fail, we die with them. But if we lose these two generals, how could we face the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」遂率鐵騎北渡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led iron cavalry north across [the river].
translations.idiomatic: He then led his armored cavalry across the river to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 敵見塵起，謂救兵至，乃引去。

translations.literal: The enemy saw dust rise and thought relief troops had arrived; thereupon they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the dust of his charge, the enemy thought reinforcements had arrived and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遂救遇與彥超而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rescued Yu and Yanchao and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He rescued Yu and Yanchao and brought them back.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嘉之，加兼侍中，移領許州，未幾，移鎮兗海。

translations.literal: The Young Emperor of Jin commended him, gave him the additional title of Palace Attendant, and shifted him to hold Xuzhou; before long, he was moved to garrison Yanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chudi praised his deed, made him concurrent Palace Attendant, and transferred him to Xuzhou; soon afterward he was posted to Yanhai.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，授襄州節度使、兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Han possessed the realm, [the court] appointed him military governor of Xiangzhou and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty held the empire, he was made military governor of Xiangzhou and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 屬荊人叛命，潛遣舟師數千屠襄、郢，審琦禦之而遁，朝廷賞功，就加守太保，進封齊國公。

translations.literal: It happened that the people of Jing rebelled against orders; [they] secretly sent several thousand river troops to slaughter Xiang and Ying; Shenqi resisted them and they fled; the court rewarded his merit, and on the spot added Grand Guardian and advanced him to Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing region rebelled, rebels secretly sent thousands of river troops to ravage Xiang and Ying. Shenqi drove them off. The court rewarded him with acting Grand Guardian and enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，又加守太傅。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was again given acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was further honored as acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 國初，封南陽王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the state, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，進封陳王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, he was advanced to Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he was raised to Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，加守太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, [Shenqi] was given acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Shenqi was made acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜章請覲，優詔許之，加守太師，增食邑至一萬五百戶，食實封二千三百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year, he submitted a memorial requesting an audience; an excellent edict permitted it; he was given acting Grand Preceptor; his fief households were increased to ten thousand five hundred, with two thousand three hundred actual enfeoffment households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized requesting an audience at court, and a gracious edict granted it. He was made acting Grand Preceptor, his nominal fief was raised to ten thousand five hundred households, and his actual enfeoffment to two thousand three hundred.

sentences.zh: 審琦鎮襄、沔僅一紀，嚴而不殘，威而不暴，故南邦之民甚懷其惠。

translations.literal: Shenqi governed Xiang and Mian for barely one twelve-year cycle; stern yet not cruel, awe-inspiring yet not violent — therefore the people of the southern states deeply cherished his grace.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi governed Xiang and Mian for nearly twelve years. He was strict but not cruel, imposing but not brutal, and the southern peoples deeply cherished his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 五年，移平盧軍節度使，承詔赴鎮，因朝於京師，世宗以國之元老，禮遇甚厚，車駕親幸其第以寵之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was moved to military governor of the Pinglu Army; he received the edict and went to his command; on the way he attended court at the capital; Shizong, because he was an elder statesman of the realm, treated him with very great courtesy; the imperial carriage personally visited his residence to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to military governor of Pinglu. En route to his post he attended court, and Shizong, honoring him as a senior pillar of the state, received him with exceptional ceremony and even visited his residence in person.

sentences.zh: 六年正月七日夜，為其隸人安友進、安萬合所害，時年六十三。

translations.literal: On the night of the seventh day of the first month of the sixth year, he was killed by his retainers An Youjin and An Wanhe; he was then sixty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the seventh day of the first month in the sixth year, his retainers An Youjin and An Wanhe murdered him. He was sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 初，友進與審琦之愛妾私通，有年數矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Youjin had carried on a secret affair with Shenqi's favorite concubine for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Youjin had been carrying on an affair with Shenqi's favorite concubine for years.

sentences.zh: 其妾常慮事泄見誅，因與友進謀害審琦，友進甚有難色。

translations.literal: That concubine constantly feared that if the affair were exposed she would be put to death; therefore together with Youjin she plotted to kill Shenqi; Youjin showed great reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: The concubine constantly feared exposure and execution, so she plotted with Youjin to kill Shenqi, though Youjin was deeply reluctant.

sentences.zh: 其妾曰：「爾若不從，我當反告。

translations.literal: That concubine said: "If you do not comply, I shall accuse you in turn."
translations.idiomatic: She told him, "If you refuse, I will accuse you instead."

sentences.zh: 」友進乃許之。

translations.literal: Youjin thereupon agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Youjin finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 至是夕，審琦沈醉，寢於帳中，其妾乃取審琦所枕劍與友進，友進猶惶駭不敢剚刃，遽召其黨安萬合，便殺審琦。

translations.literal: When that evening came, Shenqi was deeply drunk and slept in his tent; that concubine then took the sword Shenqi used as a pillow and gave it to Youjin; Youjin was still fearful and dared not stab with the blade; he hastily summoned his accomplice An Wanhe, and they killed Shenqi.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Shenqi lay drunk in his tent. The concubine took the sword he slept upon and handed it to Youjin, who was still too terrified to strike. He summoned his accomplice An Wanhe, and together they killed Shenqi.

sentences.zh: 既而慮事泄，乃引其帳下數妓，盡殺以滅其跡。

translations.literal: Afterward, fearing the affair would be exposed, they led out several singing girls under his tent and killed them all to erase the traces.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing discovery, they then summoned several entertainers from his household and killed them all to destroy the evidence.

sentences.zh: 不數日，友進等竟敗，悉為子守忠臠而戮之。

translations.literal: Within a few days, Youjin and the others were ultimately defeated; all were dismembered and executed by his son Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Youjin and his accomplices were captured and dismembered on the orders of Shenqi's son Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之震悼，輟視朝三日，詔贈尚書令，追封齊王。

translations.literal: When Shizong heard of it he was shaken and grieved; he suspended court audiences for three days; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Director of the Secretariat and pursued enfeoffment as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was shaken with grief, suspended court for three days, and ordered him posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 守忠仕皇朝，累為郡守。

translations.literal: Shouzhong served the present dynasty and repeatedly held prefectural governorships.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong served the present dynasty and held several prefectural posts in succession.

sentences.zh: 安審暉，字明遠，審琦之兄也。

translations.literal: An Shenhui, courtesy name Mingyuan, was Shenqi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: An Shenhui, whose courtesy name was Mingyuan, was Shenqi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 起家自長直軍使，轉外衙左廂軍使。

translations.literal: He began his career as commissioner of the Long Straight Army and was transferred to commander of the Left Wing of the Outer Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as commissioner of the Long Straight Army and rose to commander of the left wing of the outer guard.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗平幽、薊，戰山東，定河南，皆預其功。

translations.literal: He followed Zhuangzong in pacifying You and Ji, fought in Shandong, and settled Henan — in all he shared in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong in pacifying You and Ji, fought in Shandong, and helped secure Henan, earning distinction in each campaign.

sentences.zh: 同光中，授蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: During Tongguang, he was appointed prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era he was made prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 天成初，改汝州防禦副使，歷鳳翔徐州節度副使、河東行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, he was changed to deputy defense commissioner of Ruzhou, and successively served as deputy military governor of Fengxiang and Xuzhou and as field camp marshal of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he became deputy defense commissioner of Ruzhou, then served as deputy military governor at Fengxiang and Xuzhou and as field marshal of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖龍飛，以霸府上僚授振武兵馬留後，遷河陽節度使，不逾月移鎮鄜州，丁內艱，起復視事。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor of Jin ascended the throne, as a senior officer of the hegemon's residence he was appointed acting commander of Zhenwu horse and foot; he was moved to military governor of Heyang; within a month he was shifted to garrison Fuzhou; on his mother's mourning he was recalled from leave to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Later Jin took the throne, Shenhui was made acting commander of Zhenwu cavalry and infantry as a senior member of the founding staff. He was soon posted to Heyang, then within a month to Fuzhou. After mourning his mother he was recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 五年，李金全據安州叛，詔馬全節為都部署，領兵討之，以審暉為副。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Li Jinquan seized Anzhou in rebellion; an edict made Ma Quanjie overall deployer to lead troops to suppress him, with Shenhui as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Li Jinquan rebelled and held Anzhou. Ma Quanjie was named supreme commander to suppress him, with Shenhui as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 安睦平，移鎮鄧州，進位檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When An and Mu were pacified, he was moved to garrison Dengzhou and advanced to acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After An and Mu were pacified, he was transferred to Dengzhou and promoted to acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，襄州安從進叛，舉漢南之眾北攻南陽。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, An Congjin of Xiangzhou rebelled and raised the masses of south Han to attack Nanyang from the north.
translations.idiomatic: That winter An Congjin rebelled at Xiangzhou and marched the forces of the Han River southlands north against Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 南陽素無城壁，唯守衙城，賊傅城下，審暉登陴，召賊帥以讓之，從進不克而退。

translations.literal: Nanyang had never had city walls; they only held the yamen city; the rebels pressed against the walls; Shenhui mounted the battlements, summoned the rebel chieftain to reproach him, and Congjin could not overcome them and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang had no outer walls and held only the administrative compound. When rebels pressed the walls, Shenhui mounted the ramparts and summoned their leader to rebuke him. Congjin failed to take the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 襄州平，就加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Xiangzhou was pacified, he was on the spot given acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangzhou was pacified, he was promoted to acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，加檢校太師，罷鎮，授右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, [Shenhui] was given acting Grand Preceptor, relieved of his command, and appointed commander of the Right Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chudi succeeded, Shenhui was made acting Grand Preceptor, relieved of his provincial post, and appointed commander of the Right Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出鎮上黨，屬契丹內侵，授邢州節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he went out to garrison Shangdang; it happened that the Khitan invaded within the borders; he was appointed military governor of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was posted to Shangdang. When the Khitan raided the interior, he was made military governor of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 居無何，目疾暴作，上章求代，歸於京師，養疾累年。

translations.literal: Before long he had been there, when eye disease suddenly broke out; he submitted a memorial requesting replacement and returned to the capital, nursing his illness for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was struck by sudden blindness. He memorialized for relief, returned to the capital, and spent years convalescing.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，召於內殿，從容顧問，尤所嘆重。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor took the throne, [Shenhui] was summoned to the inner hall; with ease he was consulted, and was especially admired and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor acceded, Shenhui was summoned to the inner palace for leisurely consultation and was held in exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 將以祿起之，審暉辭以暮齒，願就頤養。

translations.literal: The court was about to raise him with salary; Shenhui declined on grounds of advanced years and wished to retire to nourishment and repose.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to recall him with an office and salary, but Shenhui declined on account of his advanced age and asked to live out his days in quiet retirement.

sentences.zh: 拜太子太師致仕，封魯國公，累食邑五千戶，實封四百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, with cumulative fief households of five thousand and four hundred actual enfeoffment households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu with a nominal fief of five thousand households and four hundred actual enfeoffment households.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年春卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of the second year of Guangshun at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 廢朝二日，詔贈侍中，謚曰靜。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for two days; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Palace Attendant; his posthumous title was Jing (Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were suspended for two days. He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant with the posthumous title Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 子守鏻，仕皇朝為贊善大夫。

translations.literal: His son Shoulian served the present dynasty as aide to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoulian served the present dynasty as aide to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 安審信，字行光，審琦之從父兄也。

translations.literal: An Shenxin, courtesy name Xingguang, was Shenqi's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: An Shenxin, whose courtesy name was Xingguang, was Shenqi's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 父金祐，世為沙陀部偏裨，名聞邊塞。

translations.literal: His father Jinyou generation after generation was a deputy commander of the Shatuo tribe, his name heard on the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinyou had for generations served as a Shatuo deputy commander, and his fame rang along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 審信習騎射。

translations.literal: Shenxin practiced riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxin trained in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 從父金全，天成初，為振武節度使，補為牙將。

translations.literal: His cousin Jinquan, at the beginning of Tiancheng, was military governor of Zhenwu; [Shenxin] was appointed as a guards officer.
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin Jinquan became military governor of Zhenwu early in Tiancheng, Shenxin was appointed to his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 俄而兄審通為滄州節度使，用為衙內都虞候，歷同、陜、許三州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Before long his elder brother Shentong became military governor of Cangzhou and employed him as chief military adviser within the yamen; he successively served as commander of horse and foot at Tong, Shan, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his elder brother Shentong became military governor of Cangzhou and made him chief adjutant of the headquarters. He later commanded the horse and foot forces at Tong, Shan, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 晉祖起義於太原，唐末帝命張敬達以兵攻之，而審信率先以部下兵遁入并州，晉祖以其故人，得之甚悅。

translations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor raised righteousness at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor of Tang ordered Zhang Jingda to attack with troops; Shenxin was the first to lead the troops under his command in flight into Bingzhou; the Jin Ancestor, because he was an old acquaintance, was greatly pleased to obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rebelled at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor sent Zhang Jingda against him. Shenxin was the first to desert with his troops to Bingzhou. Gaozu, delighted to see an old acquaintance, received him warmly.

sentences.zh: 其妻與二子在京師，皆為唐末帝所戮，但貸其老母而已。

translations.literal: His wife and two sons were in the capital; all were executed by the Last Emperor of Tang; only his aged mother was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and two sons were in the capital and were all executed by the Last Emperor. Only his elderly mother was spared.

sentences.zh: 契丹既降晉安寨，晉高祖以審信為汾州刺史、檢校太保，充馬步軍副部署。

translations.literal: After the Khitan had reduced Jin'an Stockade, the High Ancestor of Jin made Shenxin prefect of Fenzhou and acting Grand Guardian, and made him deputy deployer of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan reduced Jin'an Stockade, Gaozu made Shenxin prefect of Fenzhou and acting Grand Guardian and appointed him deputy commander of the horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 晉祖入洛，授河中節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor entered Luoyang, [Shenxin] was appointed military governor of Hezhong, acting Grand Commandant, and Grand Councillor of the State Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Shenxin was made military governor of Hezhong, acting Grand Commandant, and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 審信性既翻覆，率多疑忌，在蒲中時，每王人告諭，騎從稍多，必潛設備，以防其圖己。

translations.literal: Shenxin's nature was changeable and he was by habit suspicious; when at Puzhong, whenever imperial envoys came to instruct him, if their mounted escort was even slightly numerous, he would secretly make preparations against them plotting against himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxin was fickle and habitually suspicious. At Puzhong, whenever imperial envoys arrived, if their escort was at all large he secretly took precautions, fearing a plot against his life.

sentences.zh: 尋歷許、兗州鎮，所至以聚斂為務，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Before long he successively governed Xu and Yan; wherever he went he made exaction his business, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted to Xu and Yan, where he devoted himself to extortion and the people suffered deeply.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷謀大舉北伐，凡藩侯皆預將帥，以審信為馬步軍右廂都排陣使，俄改華州節度使。

translations.literal: It happened that the court planned a great northern campaign; all frontier lords were included among the commanders; Shenxin was made array marshal of the right wing of horse and foot; before long he was changed to military governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court planned a major northern campaign, all military governors were enlisted as commanders. Shenxin was made array marshal of the right wing of the horse and foot armies, then was soon transferred to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 漢初，移鎮同州，入為左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he was moved to garrison Tongzhou and entered [court] as general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty he was posted to Tongzhou, then summoned to court as general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 國初，轉右金吾上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the state, he was transferred to general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he became general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年夏四月，太祖禦乾元殿入閣，審信不赴班位，為御史所彈，詔釋之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the third year, the founding emperor held court at the Qianyuan Hall for entering the pavilion; Shenxin did not attend his place in the ranks; he was impeached by the censorate; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year the founding emperor held court at the Qianyuan Hall. Shenxin failed to take his place in the ranks and was impeached by the censorate, but an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 時審信久病，神情恍惚，聞臺司奏劾，揚言曰：「趨朝偶晚，未是大過，何用彈舉！

translations.literal: At that time Shenxin had long been ill, his spirit and expression dazed; hearing the censorate's impeachment, he proclaimed aloud: "Arriving at court a little late is not a great fault — why impeach!"
translations.idiomatic: Shenxin had been ill for a long time and was mentally clouded. Hearing of the impeachment, he declared aloud, "Being a little late to court is no great crime. Why impeach me?"

sentences.zh: 我終進奉二萬緡，盡逐此乞索兒輩。

translations.literal: I will in the end present twenty thousand strings of cash and drive out all these beggar fellows.
translations.idiomatic: I will pay twenty thousand strings of cash and have every one of these beggars driven out.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，以病請退，授太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: Before long, on grounds of illness he requested retirement and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he requested retirement on grounds of illness and was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋卒，年六十。

translations.literal: That autumn he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died that autumn at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，謚曰成穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Palace Attendant; his posthumous title was Chengmù (Accomplished and Solemn).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant with the posthumous title Accomplished and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 李從敏，字叔達，唐明宗之猶子也。

translations.literal: Li Congmin, courtesy name Shuda, was a nephew of Emperor Mingzong of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congmin, whose courtesy name was Shuda, was a nephew of Emperor Mingzong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 沈厚寡言，善騎射，多計數。

translations.literal: He was deep and thick, sparing of speech, skilled at riding and archery, and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and taciturn, an expert horseman and archer, and adept at calculation.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗召見，試弓馬，用為衙內馬軍指揮使，從平汴、洛，補帳前都指揮使，遷捧聖都將。

translations.literal: At first Zhuangzong summoned him for an audience, tested his bow and horse, and employed him as commander of the guards' cavalry; he followed in pacifying Bian and Luo, was appointed commander before the tent, and was promoted to colonel of the Upholding the Sage [Army].
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong first summoned him, tested his horsemanship and archery, and made him commander of the guard cavalry. He followed the conquest of Bian and Luoyang, became commander of the imperial tent guard, and was promoted colonel of the Upholding the Sage Army.

sentences.zh: 明宗移鎮真定，表為成德軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was shifted to garrison Zhending, he memorialized [Congmin] as commander of the Chengde Army's horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was transferred to Zhending, he recommended Congmin as commander of the Chengde horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 從明宗入洛，補皇城使，出為陜府節度使。

translations.literal: He followed Mingzong into Luoyang, was appointed commissioner of the Imperial City, and went out as military governor of the Shan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Mingzong to Luoyang, became commissioner of the Imperial City, and was then sent out as military governor of Shan.

sentences.zh: 王都據定州叛，命王晏球為招討使，率師討之，以從敏為副，領滄州節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Du held Dingzhou in rebellion; [the court] appointed Wang Yanqiu as suppression commissioner to lead troops against him, with Congmin as deputy and holding the military governorship of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Du rebelled and held Dingzhou, Wang Yanqiu was named suppression commissioner with Congmin as his deputy, while Congmin also held the military governorship of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王都平，移授定州。

translations.literal: When Wang Du was pacified, [Congmin] was transferred and appointed to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Du was defeated, Congmin was transferred to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋代範延光為成德軍節度使，加檢校太尉，封涇王。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Fan Yanguang as military governor of the Chengde Army, was given acting Grand Commandant, and enfeoffed as Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Fan Yanguang as military governor of Chengde, was made acting Grand Commandant, and enfeoffed as Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 鎮州有市人劉方遇，家富於財。

translations.literal: In Zhenzhou there was a townsman Liu Fangyu, whose family was rich in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenzhou there lived a merchant named Liu Fangyu, whose family was very wealthy.

sentences.zh: 方遇卒，無子。

translations.literal: Fangyu died without a son.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu died without a son.

sentences.zh: 妻弟田令遵者，幼為方遇治財，善殖貨，劉族乃共推令遵為方遇子，親族共立券書，以為誓信。

translations.literal: His wife's younger brother Tian Lingzun, from youth had managed Fangyu's finances and was skilled at multiplying goods; the Liu clan thereupon jointly promoted Lingzun as Fangyu's son; kinsmen together drew up a bond as sworn pledge.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's younger brother Tian Lingzun had managed Fangyu's finances since youth and was skilled at trade. The Liu clan agreed to adopt Lingzun as Fangyu's heir, and the relatives drew up a written pledge to seal the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 累年後，方遇二女取資於令遵不如意，乃訟令遵冒姓，奪父家財，從敏令判官陸浣鞫其獄，而殺令遵。

translations.literal: After many years, Fangyu's two daughters, dissatisfied with receiving funds from Lingzun, thereupon sued that Lingzun had falsely taken the surname and seized their father's family wealth; Congmin ordered his judicial officer Lu Huan to try the case and killed Lingzun.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Fangyu's two daughters, unhappy with the payments they received from Lingzun, sued him for falsely assuming the Liu surname and seizing their father's estate. Congmin had his judicial officer Lu Huan try the case and executed Lingzun.

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》云：鎮州市人劉方遇，家財數十萬。

translations.literal: (The Beimeng Suoyan says: The townsman Liu Fangyu of Zhenzhou had family wealth of several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: (Beimeng Suoyan: Liu Fangyu, a merchant of Zhenzhou, possessed family wealth of several hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 方遇妻田氏蚤卒，田之妹為尼，常出入方遇家，方遇使尼長發為繼室。

translations.literal: Fangyu's wife, née Tian, died early; Tian's younger sister was a nun who often came and went in Fangyu's household; Fangyu had the nun let her hair grow long and made her his successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu's wife, née Tian, died young. Her younger sister was a nun who often visited the Fang household, and Fangyu had her grow out her hair and made her his second wife.

sentences.zh: 有田令遵者，方遇之妻弟也，善貨殖，方遇以所積財令令遵興殖焉。

translations.literal: There was Tian Lingzun, Fangyu's wife's younger brother, skilled at trade; Fangyu entrusted the wealth he had accumulated to Lingzun to expand through commerce.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzun, Fangyu's brother-in-law, was skilled at trade, and Fangyu entrusted his accumulated wealth to Lingzun to invest and expand.

sentences.zh: 方遇有子年幼，二女皆嫁。

translations.literal: Fangyu had a young son; both daughters were married.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu had a young son, and both daughters were already married.

sentences.zh: 方遇疾卒，子幼不能督家業，方遇妻及二女以家財素為令遵興殖，乃聚族合謀，請以令遵姓劉，為方遇繼嗣，即令鬻券人安美為親族請嗣。

translations.literal: Fangyu died suddenly of illness; the son was young and could not oversee the family business; Fangyu's wife and two daughters, because the family wealth had always been expanded by Lingzun, thereupon gathered the clan in joint plot and requested that Lingzun take the surname Liu as Fangyu's successor heir; they then had An Mei, who had sold the bond, petition the kin as relatives for the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu died suddenly. His son was too young to manage the estate. Because the family wealth had long been built up by Lingzun, the wife and two daughters gathered the clan and agreed to have Lingzun take the Liu surname as Fangyu's heir. An Mei, who had drawn up the bond, was sent to petition the authorities on behalf of the kin.

sentences.zh: 券書既定，乃遣令遵服斬衰居喪。

translations.literal: Once the bond was settled, they then had Lingzun wear the hemmed sackcloth of mourning and observe the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Once the bond was signed, Lingzun was made to wear mourning garments and observe the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 而二女初立令遵時，先邀每月供財二萬，及後求取無厭，而石、李二女夫使二女詣本府論訴，雲令遵冒姓，奪父家財，令遵下獄。

translations.literal: When the two daughters first established Lingzun, they had first demanded twenty thousand in monthly support; afterward their demands were insatiable; then the husbands of the Shi and Li daughters had the two daughters go to the headquarters to argue and sue, saying Lingzun had falsely taken the surname and seized their father's family wealth; Lingzun was put in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzun was first installed, the daughters had demanded twenty thousand per month in support, but their demands soon became insatiable. The husbands of the Shi and Li daughters then sent them to the headquarters to sue, claiming Lingzun had falsely assumed the Liu name and seized the family estate. Lingzun was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 石、李二夫族與本府要吏親黨，上至府帥判官、行軍司馬、隨使都押衙，各受方遇二女賂錢數千緡，而以令遵與姊及書券安美同情共盜，俱棄市，人知其冤。）〉

translations.literal: The Shi and Li husbands' clans were kin to key officials of the headquarters; from the commandery judge and field camp marshal down to the chief escort officer of the attendant mission, each received several thousand strings in bribes from Fangyu's two daughters; and on the charge that Lingzun, his elder sister, and An Mei who wrote the bond were accomplices in joint theft, all were executed in the marketplace; people knew it was wrongful.)]
translations.idiomatic: The Shi and Li families were connected to key officials of the headquarters, from the commandery judge and field marshal down to the chief escort officer. Each received thousands of strings in bribes from Fangyu's daughters. Lingzun, his elder sister, and An Mei, who had drawn up the bond, were convicted as accomplices in theft and executed in the marketplace. All who knew the case recognized it as a gross injustice.)]

sentences.zh: 令遵父詣臺訴冤，詔本州節度副使符蒙、掌書記徐臺符鞫之，備明奸狀。

translations.literal: Lingzun's father went to the censorate to plead the injustice; an edict ordered the deputy military governor of this prefecture Fu Meng and recorder Xu Taifu to try the case, fully clarifying the corrupt circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzun's father appealed to the censorate. An edict ordered the deputy military governor Fu Meng and recorder Xu Taifu to investigate, and they fully exposed the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 及詰二女，伏行賂於節度使趙環、代判高知柔、觀察判官陸浣，並捕下獄，具服贓罪。

translations.literal: When the two daughters were interrogated, they confessed to bribing the military governor Zhao Huan, acting judge Gao Zhirou, and surveillance judicial officer Lu Huan; all were arrested and imprisoned and fully confessed their bribery crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation the two daughters confessed to bribing the military governor Zhao Huan, acting judge Gao Zhirou, and surveillance judicial officer Lu Huan. All were arrested, imprisoned, and confessed to bribery.

sentences.zh: 事連從敏，甚懼，乃令其妻赴洛陽，入宮告王淑妃。

translations.literal: The affair implicated Congmin; he was greatly afraid and thereupon had his wife go to Luoyang and enter the palace to inform Consort Wang Shufei.
translations.idiomatic: The case implicated Congmin, who was terrified. He sent his wife to Luoyang to appeal to Consort Wang Shufei in the palace.

sentences.zh: 明宗知之，怒曰：「朕用從敏為節度使，而枉法殺人，我羞見百官，又令新婦奔赴，不須見吾面。

translations.literal: When Mingzong learned of it he was angry and said: "I employed Congmin as military governor, yet he killed people in violation of law — I am ashamed to face the hundred officials; moreover you send a new wife to plead — she need not see my face."
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong learned of it he was furious. "I made Congmin a military governor, and he kills men in defiance of the law. I am ashamed to face my officials. And now you send your new wife to plead for you? She need not come before me."

sentences.zh: 」時王淑妃頗庇護之，趙環等三人竟棄市，從敏等止於罰俸而已。

translations.literal: At that time Consort Wang Shufei rather protected him; Zhao Huan and the other three were ultimately executed in the marketplace; Congmin and the others were only fined a year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang Shufei intervened on his behalf. Zhao Huan and the other two officials were executed in the marketplace, while Congmin and his associates were merely fined a year's salary.

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：從敏初欲削官，中宮哀祈，竟罰一年俸。）〉

translations.literal: (Beimeng Suoyan: Congmin at first was to be stripped of office; the inner palace pleaded in grief; in the end he was fined one year's salary.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Beimeng Suoyan: Congmin was at first to be stripped of office, but the inner palace pleaded on his behalf, and in the end he was fined only one year's salary.)]

sentences.zh: 鄭仁誨，字日新，晉陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Renhui, courtesy name Rixin, was a man of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Renhui, whose courtesy name was Rixin, came from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 父霸，累贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His father Ba was repeatedly enfeoffed posthumously as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ba was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 仁誨幼事唐驍將陳紹光，恃勇使酒，嘗乘醉抽佩劍，將事刂刃於仁誨，左右無不奔避，唯仁誨端立以俟，略無懼色。

translations.literal: Renhui in youth served the Tang fierce general Chen Shaoguang, who relied on courage and indulged in wine; once when drunk he drew his girdle sword and was about to test the blade on Renhui; those at his side all fled in avoidance; only Renhui stood upright waiting, with no sign of fear.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Renhui served the Tang general Chen Shaoguang, a man who relied on his courage and drank heavily. Once, drunk, Chen drew his sword to test its edge on Renhui. Everyone fled, but Renhui stood upright and waited without the slightest fear.

sentences.zh: 紹光因擲劍於地，謂仁誨曰：「汝有此器度，必當享人間富貴。

translations.literal: Shaoguang thereupon cast the sword to the ground and said to Renhui: "You have this breadth of character — you are sure to enjoy human wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoguang threw down his sword and told Renhui, "A man of your bearing is destined for wealth and high office."

sentences.zh: 」及紹光典郡，仁誨累為右職。

translations.literal: When Shaoguang governed a prefecture, Renhui repeatedly held senior posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoguang governed a prefecture, Renhui rose through several senior posts.

sentences.zh: 後退歸鄉里，以色養為樂。

translations.literal: Later he retired to his home district and took delight in supporting his parents with finery and food.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired to his home district and devoted himself to caring for his parents.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖之鎮河東也，太祖累就其第，與之燕語，每有質問，無不以正理為答，太祖深器之。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor of Han governed Hedong, the founding emperor repeatedly visited his residence and conversed with him at ease; whenever there were questions, [Renhui] answered without fail by right principle; the founding emperor deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Han governed Hedong, the future founding emperor often visited his home for leisurely conversation. Whatever question was raised, Renhui answered with sound principle, and the founding emperor came to esteem him deeply.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，太祖初領樞務，即召為從職。

translations.literal: When Han possessed the realm, as soon as the founding emperor first took charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he summoned [Renhui] as an attendant officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty held the empire and the founding emperor first took charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Renhui was summoned as an attendant officer.

sentences.zh: 及太祖西征，嘗密贊軍機，西師凱旋，累遷至檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor campaigned west, [Renhui] secretly assisted in military planning; when the western army returned in triumph, he was repeatedly promoted to acting Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the founding emperor's western campaign Renhui secretly advised on military affairs. After the victorious return he was promoted to acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，旌佐命功，授檢校司空、客省使兼大內都點檢、恩州團練使，尋為樞密副使。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor ascended the throne, he honored merit in assisting the mandate and appointed [Renhui] acting Minister of Works, commissioner of the Reception Bureau and concurrent chief inspector of the Great Inner Palace, regimental commissioner of Enzhou; before long he became deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took the throne he rewarded Renhui's service in establishing the dynasty with acting Minister of Works, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, chief inspector of the inner palace, and regimental commissioner of Enzhou. He soon became deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 逾年轉宣徽北院使、右衛大將軍，出鎮澶淵，轉檢校太保，入為樞密使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat and general of the Right Guard; he went out to garrison Chanzhou; was transferred to acting Grand Guardian; entered [court] as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was given Grand Councillor of the State Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat and general of the Right Guard, then was posted to Chanzhou and promoted to acting Grand Guardian. He returned to court as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 世宗之北征也，以仁誨為東京留守，調發軍須，供億無所闕，駕回，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned north, he made Renhui regent of the Eastern Capital; [Renhui] mobilized military supplies and provisions without any lack; when the imperial carriage returned, [he] was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Shizong's northern campaign Renhui served as regent of the Eastern Capital and mobilized supplies without shortfall. When the emperor returned, Renhui was made concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋丁內艱，未幾起復。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his mother; before long he was recalled from leave.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his mother and was shortly recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年冬，疾亟，世宗幸其第，親加撫問，欷歔久之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xiande, his illness was critical; Shizong visited his residence and personally comforted and inquired after him, sighing and sobbing for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Xiande his illness grew critical. Shizong visited his home in person to comfort him and wept for a long while.

sentences.zh: 及卒，世宗親臨其喪，哭逾數舉。

translations.literal: When he died, Shizong personally attended his funeral and wept beyond several rounds of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Shizong attended the funeral in person and wept repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 是時，世宗將行，近臣奏云：「歲道非便，不宜臨喪。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong was about to depart; close ministers memorialized saying: "The year's course is not favorable — it is not fitting to attend the funeral in person."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was about to depart on campaign when close advisers urged him, "The astrological season is unfavorable. You should not attend the funeral in person."

sentences.zh: 」弗聽，然而先之以桃茢之事，時以為得禮。

translations.literal: He did not listen; yet he first performed the peach-branch and reed-sweep rites; at the time this was considered proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He paid no heed, but first performed the peach-branch purification rites. Contemporaries considered this proper observance of ritual.

sentences.zh: 仁誨為人端厚謙損，造次必由於禮。

translations.literal: Renhui as a man was upright, thick, humble, and modest; in every hasty act he necessarily followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Renhui was upright, modest, and humble. Even in haste he always acted according to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 及居樞務，雖權位崇重，而能孜孜接物，無自矜之色，至終，故朝廷鹹惜之。

translations.literal: When he held the Bureau of Military Affairs, although his power and position were lofty and weighty, he could diligently receive others without any self-congratulatory bearing, to the end; therefore the court all cherished and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held great power as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he remained diligent in dealing with others and never showed arrogance to the end. The entire court mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 詔贈中書令，追封韓國公，謚曰忠正。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Director of the Secretariat, pursued enfeoffment as Duke of Han, posthumous title Zhongzheng (Loyal and Upright).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Han, with the posthumous title Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 既葬，命翰林學士陶穀撰神道碑文，官為建立，表特恩也。

translations.literal: After burial, [the court] ordered Hanlin academician Tao Gu to compose the spirit-way stele inscription; officials erected it — a mark of special grace.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial the court ordered Hanlin academician Tao Gu to compose the spirit-way stele inscription and had officials erect it, a mark of special imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 子勛，累歷內職，蚤卒，絕嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xun successively held inner-court posts, died young, and left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun held several inner-court posts but died young without heirs.

sentences.zh: 初，廣順末，王殷受詔赴闕，太祖遣仁誨赴鄴都巡檢，及殷得罪，仁誨不奉詔即殺其子，蓋利其家財妓樂也。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Guangshun, Wang Yin received an edict to proceed to court; the founding emperor sent Renhui to Ye for inspection; when Yin was found guilty, Renhui without awaiting the edict killed his son — presumably coveting his family's wealth, singing girls, and musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guangshun, when Wang Yin was summoned to court, the founding emperor sent Renhui to inspect Ye. When Yin fell from favor, Renhui killed Yin's son without awaiting orders, apparently to seize his family's wealth, entertainers, and musicians.

sentences.zh: 及仁誨卒而無後，人以為陰責焉。

translations.literal: When Renhui died without posterity, people regarded it as hidden retribution.
translations.idiomatic: When Renhui died without heirs, people regarded it as karmic retribution.

sentences.zh: 張彥成，潞州潞城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yancheng was a man of Lucheng in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yancheng came from Lucheng in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖靜，汾州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jing was prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jing had been prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖述，澤州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shu was prefect of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shu had been prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 父礪，昭義行軍司馬。

translations.literal: His father Li was field camp marshal of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li had served as field marshal of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 彥成初為並門牙將。

translations.literal: Yancheng at first was a guards officer at the Bing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yancheng began as a guards officer at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天成中，自秦州鹽鐵務官改鄆州都押牙。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, from salt and iron commissioner at Qinzhou he was changed to chief escort officer at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he moved from salt and iron commissioner at Qinzhou to chief escort officer at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢祖鎮北門，表為行軍司馬，以隱帝娶其女，特見親愛。

translations.literal: When the Han Ancestor garrisoned the North Gate, he memorialized [Yancheng] as field camp marshal; because the Hidden Emperor married his daughter, [Yancheng] was especially shown affection.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Han governed the northern gate he recommended Yancheng as field marshal. Because Emperor Yindi married his daughter, Yancheng enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 從平汴、洛，累加特進、檢校太尉、同州節度使。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Bian and Luo, was repeatedly given special advancement, acting Grand Commandant, and military governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the conquest of Bian and Luoyang and was repeatedly honored with special advancement, acting Grand Commandant, and the military governorship of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，就加同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor took the throne, [Yancheng] was on the spot given Grand Councillor of the State Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yindi acceded, Yancheng was made Grand Councillor on the spot.

sentences.zh: 太祖之伐河中，彥成有饋免之勞，河中平，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor campaigned against Hezhong, Yancheng had the merit of supplying provisions and exemption; when Hezhong was pacified, [he] was given acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor campaigned against Hezhong, Yancheng earned merit by supplying provisions. After Hezhong fell he was made acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬，移鎮相州。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Qianyou, he was moved to garrison Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Qianyou he was transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，就加兼侍中，尋移鎮南陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he was on the spot given concurrent Palace Attendant; before long he was moved to garrison Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was made concurrent Palace Attendant, then was soon posted to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，代歸，授右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, he was replaced and returned, and was appointed general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year he was recalled and appointed general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，以疾卒，年六十。

translations.literal: That autumn he died of illness, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died of illness at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·楊克讓傳》：乾祐中，同州節度使張彥成表授掌書記。

translations.literal: (Biography of Yang Kerang in the History of Song: During Qianyou, the military governor of Tongzhou Zhang Yancheng memorialized to appoint him recorder.)
translations.idiomatic: (History of Song, Biography of Yang Kerang: During Qianyou, Zhang Yancheng, military governor of Tongzhou, recommended him as recorder.)

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，彥成移鎮安陽、穰下，克讓以奮職從行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun in Zhou, Yancheng was moved to garrison Anyang and Rangxia; Kerang followed in diligent discharge of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Guangshun, when Yancheng was transferred to Anyang and Rangxia, Kerang accompanied him in diligent service.

sentences.zh: 彥成入為執金吾，病篤，奏稱其材可用。

translations.literal: Yancheng entered [court] as Bearer of the Golden Mace; critically ill, he memorialized that Kerang's talent could be employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yancheng entered court as Bearer of the Golden Mace and fell gravely ill, he memorialized that Kerang's talents should be employed.

sentences.zh: 克讓以彥成死未葬，不忍就祿，退居別墅，俟張氏子外除，時論稱之。）〉

translations.literal: Kerang, because Yancheng had died and was not yet buried, could not bear to accept salary; he retired to a separate villa and waited until the Zhang family's mourning period of seclusion ended; public opinion praised him.)]
translations.idiomatic: Because Yancheng had died and was not yet buried, Kerang could not bring himself to accept office. He retired to a villa and waited until the Zhang family's mourning period ended. Public opinion praised his conduct.)]

sentences.zh: 安叔千，沙陀三部落之種也。

translations.literal: An Shuqian was of the stock of the three Shatuo tribal confederations.
translations.idiomatic: An Shuqian came from the three Shatuo tribal confederations.

sentences.zh: 父懷盛，事唐武皇，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: His father Huaisheng served the Martial Emperor of Tang and was known for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaisheng served Li Keyong and was renowned for martial valor.

sentences.zh: 叔千習騎射，從莊宗定河南為奉安部將。

translations.literal: Shuqian practiced riding and archery; he followed Zhuangzong in settling Henan and became a colonel of the Pacifying and Securing [Army].
translations.idiomatic: Shuqian trained in horsemanship and archery. He followed Zhuangzong in pacifying Henan and became a colonel of the Pacifying and Securing Army.

sentences.zh: 天成初，王師伐定州，命為先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, when the imperial army campaigned against Dingzhou, he was appointed vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng, during the campaign against Dingzhou, he was appointed vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 王都平，授秦州刺史，連判涿、易二郡。

translations.literal: When Wang Du was pacified, [Shuqian] was appointed prefect of Qinzhou and concurrently judged Zhuo and Yi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Du was defeated, Shuqian was made prefect of Qinzhou and concurrently administered Zhuo and Yi.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，契丹寇雁門，叔千從晉祖迎戰，敗之，進位檢校太保、振武節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, when the Khitan raided Yanmen, Shuqian followed the Jin Ancestor to meet them in battle and defeated them; he was advanced to acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai, when the Khitan raided Yanmen, Shuqian joined Gaozu in battle and routed them. He was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 晉祖踐阼，就加同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Jin Ancestor ascended the throne, [Shuqian] was on the spot given Grand Councillor of the State Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Shuqian was made Grand Councillor on the spot.

sentences.zh: 天福中，歷邠、滄、邢、晉四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: During Tianfu, he successively served as military governor of the four commands Bin, Cang, Xing, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he served in succession as military governor of Bin, Cang, Xing, and Jin.

sentences.zh: 叔千鄙野而無文，當時謂之「安沒字」，言若碑碣之無篆籀，但虛有其表耳。

translations.literal: Shuqian was rustic and without culture; at the time they called him "An No-Characters," meaning like a stele without seal script — merely empty show.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqian was uncouth and illiterate. People called him "An No-Characters," likening him to a stele without inscription — all appearance and no substance.

sentences.zh: 開運初，朝廷將大舉北伐，授行營都排陣使，俄改左金吾衛上將軍。
