translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun, when the court was about to launch a great northern campaign, he was appointed overall array marshal of the field camp; before long he was changed to general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun, as the court prepared a major northern campaign, he was made overall array marshal of the field army, then was soon transferred to general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，百僚迎見於赤崗，契丹主登高岡駐馬而撫諭漢官，叔千出班國語，契丹主曰：「爾是安沒字否？

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, the hundred officials welcomed them at Chigang; the Khitan sovereign mounted a high hill, halted his horse, and comforted and instructed the Han officials; Shuqian stepped forward in the national language; the Khitan sovereign said: "Are you An No-Characters?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took Bian, the officials welcomed them at Chigang. The Khitan emperor halted on a hill to address the Han officials. Shuqian stepped forward speaking Khitan. The emperor said, "Are you An No-Characters?"

sentences.zh: 卿比在邢州日，遠輸誠款，我至此，汝管取一吃飯處。

translations.literal: When you were at Xingzhou, you sent sincere pledges from afar; now that I have come here, you are sure to get a place to eat your fill.
translations.idiomatic: When you were at Xingzhou you sent me loyal pledges from afar. Now that I am here, you shall have your fill of rewards.

sentences.zh: 」叔千拜謝而退，俄授鎮國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shuqian bowed in thanks and withdrew; before long he was appointed military governor of the Pacifying the State Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqian bowed in thanks and withdrew. He was soon appointed military governor of the Pacifying the State Army.

sentences.zh: 漢初，遇代歸京，自以嘗附幕庭，居常愧惕，久之，授太子太師致仕，尋請告歸洛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, when the dynasty changed and he returned to the capital, he himself felt he had once attached himself to the Khitan court and constantly lived in shame and apprehension; after a long time he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement; before long he requested leave to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty, when the regime changed and he returned to the capital, he felt ashamed for having once served the Khitan court and lived in constant unease. In time he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement and soon requested leave to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年冬卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Guangshun he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the second year of Guangshun at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 宋彥筠，雍丘人也。

translations.literal: Song Yanyun was a man of Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yanyun came from Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 初隸滑州軍，梁氏與莊宗夾河之戰，彥筠時為戰棹都指揮使，以勞遷開封府牙校。

translations.literal: At first he was attached to the Huazhou army; in the Liang and Zhuangzong's battles on opposite banks of the river, Yanyun was then commander of war boats; for his labor he was transferred to guards officer of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in the Huazhou army. During the Liang–Zhuangzong battles along the Yellow River he commanded war boats and was promoted to a guards officer of Kaifeng for his service.

sentences.zh: 莊宗有天下，擢領禁軍。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong possessed the realm, [Yanyun] was promoted to command the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong won the empire, Yanyun was promoted to command the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 伐蜀之役，率所部從康延孝為前鋒，蜀平，歷維、渝二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Shu, he led the troops under his command following Kang Yanxiao as vanguard; when Shu was pacified, he successively held the prefectures of Wei and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shu campaign he led his troops as vanguard under Kang Yanxiao. After Shu fell he served in succession as prefect of Wei and Yu.

sentences.zh: 明宗在位，連典數郡。

translations.literal: While Mingzong held the throne, [Yanyun] successively governed several prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: During Mingzong's reign he governed several prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 晉初，自汝州防禦使討安從進於襄陽，以功拜鄧州節度使，累官至檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, from defense commissioner of Ruzhou he campaigned against An Congjin at Xiangyang; for merit he was appointed military governor of Dengzhou and rose in office to acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin dynasty, as defense commissioner of Ruzhou he campaigned against An Congjin at Xiangyang. For his merit he was made military governor of Dengzhou and rose to acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，歷晉、陜二鎮。

translations.literal: Before long, he successively governed the two commands Jin and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served in succession at Jin and Shan.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，再領鄧州，尋移鎮河中。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor of Jin succeeded, [Yanyun] again held Dengzhou; before long he was moved to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chudi succeeded, Yanyun again held Dengzhou, then was soon transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 漢初，授太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.

sentences.zh: 國初，拜左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the state, he was appointed general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was made general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，復為太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, [Yanyun] again became Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong acceded, Yanyun again became Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in retirement.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年冬，卒於西京之私第。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Xiande, he died at his private residence in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the fourth year of Xiande at his private residence in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝一日，詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for one day; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，彥筠入成都，據一甲第，第中資貨鉅萬，妓女數十輩，盡為其所有。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanyun entered Chengdu, he seized a grand mansion; within the mansion goods worth tens of thousands, and several dozen singing girls — all became his possessions.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanyun entered Chengdu he seized a grand mansion stocked with wealth worth tens of thousands and dozens of entertainers, all of which became his.

sentences.zh: 一旦，與其主母微忿，遽擊殺之，自後常有所睹，彥筠心不自安，乃修浮屠法以禳之，因而溺誌於釋氏。

translations.literal: One day, having a slight quarrel with the lady of the house, he suddenly struck and killed her; afterward he often had visions; Yanyun's heart was not at ease; thereupon he practiced Buddhist rites to exorcise them, and thereby became infatuated with the Buddha's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: One day, after a minor quarrel with the lady of the house, he suddenly killed her. Thereafter he was haunted by visions and grew uneasy. He turned to Buddhist rites for exorcism and became obsessed with the faith.

sentences.zh: 其後，每歲至金仙入涅之日，常衣斬缞號慟於其像前，其佞佛也如是。

translations.literal: Afterward, every year on the day of the Golden Immortal's entry into nirvana, he regularly wore hemmed sackcloth and wailed before his image — such was his devotion to Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Every year on the anniversary of the Buddha's nirvana he donned mourning garments and wailed before the Buddha's image. Such was his fanatical devotion.

sentences.zh: 家有侍婢數十人，皆令削髮披緇，以侍左右，大為當時所誚。

translations.literal: In his household were several dozen serving maids; he had them all shave their heads and don black robes to attend at his side — greatly mocked by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He had dozens of maidservants shave their heads and don monastic robes to attend him, to the great ridicule of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 又性好貨殖，能圖什一之利，良田甲第，相望於郡國。

translations.literal: Moreover he was fond of trade and multiplication of goods by nature and could seek a ten-percent profit; fine fields and grand mansions stretched in sight across the commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a passion for commerce and could turn a ten-percent profit. Fine estates and grand mansions dotted the provinces under his control.

sentences.zh: 將終，以伊、洛之間田莊十數區上進，並籍於官焉。

translations.literal: As he was about to die, he presented more than ten estates between the Yi and Luo rivers to the throne, and all were registered to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he presented more than ten estates between the Yi and Luo to the throne, and all were registered as state property.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：近代領戎藩，列王爵，祿厚而君子不議，望重而人主不疑，能自晦於飲酌之間，保功名於始終之際，如行周之比者，幾何人哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In recent times to command military provinces and rank among princes, with thick salary yet gentlemen not criticizing, with heavy prestige yet the ruler not doubting, able to conceal oneself amid drinking, and preserve fame and merit from beginning to end — like one comparable to Xingzhou, how many men are there!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In recent times, how many men have held frontier commands and princely rank, enjoyed lavish emoluments without drawing censure, wielded great prestige without arousing suspicion, kept themselves unobtrusive amid feasting, and preserved their fame from first to last — men comparable to Xingzhou?

sentences.zh: 奕世藩翰，固亦宜然。

translations.literal: Generation after generation as frontier pillars — this is indeed as it should be.
translations.idiomatic: For a family to serve generation after generation as pillars of the frontier — that is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 審琦有分閫之勞，乏禦家之道，峰摧玉折，蓋不幸也。

translations.literal: Shenqi had the merit of sharing command of a province but lacked the way of governing a household; peak shattered, jade broken — this was surely misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi had the merit of frontier command but lacked the art of governing his household. That his peak was shattered and jade broken was surely misfortune.

sentences.zh: 其餘雖擁戎旃，未聞閫政，固不足與文、召、龔、黃為比也。

translations.literal: The rest, although they held military banners, were not heard of in provincial governance — they are indeed not fit to be compared with Wen, Shao, Gong, and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: The others, though they bore military banners, left no mark in provincial governance and cannot be compared with the likes of Duke Wen of Jin, Duke Shao of Zhou, Gongye Chang, or Huang Xian.
